outputs.L2:
A decorative sheet is provided with a transparent resin layer that combines high transparency with excellent resistance to post-processing. In one embodiment of the invention, the decorative sheet (1) includes a transparent resin layer (4) whose principal constituent is a crystalline polypropylene resin. The transparent resin layer (4) has a peak intensity ratio \(x\) of 0.65 or less, as defined by Equation (1):

\[
x=\frac{I_{997}-I_{938}}{I_{973}-I_{938}} \tag{1}
\]

The values \(I_{997}\), \(I_{938}\), and \(I_{973}\) are peak intensities calculated from the absorption spectrum of the transparent resin layer obtained through Fourier-transform infrared spectrometry. Specifically, \(I_{997}\), \(I_{938}\), and \(I_{973}\) represent the peak intensities at wavenumbers of 997 cm\(^{-1}\), 938 cm\(^{-1}\), and 973 cm\(^{-1}\), respectively.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a decorative sheet that combines excellent post-processing resistance with high transparency. The decorative sheet includes a transparent resin layer composed primarily of a crystalline polypropylene resin. This transparent resin layer has a peak intensity ratio, \(x\), of 0.65 or less, as determined from an absorption spectrum obtained by Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry.

The peak intensity ratio \(x\) is calculated according to the following formula:

\[
x = \frac{I_{997} - I_{938}}{I_{973} - I_{938}}
\]

In this formula, \(I_{997}\), \(I_{938}\), and \(I_{973}\) represent the peak intensities measured at wavenumbers of 997 cm⁻¹, 938 cm⁻¹, and 973 cm⁻¹, respectively. By controlling the peak intensity ratio within the specified range, the decorative sheet achieves both high transparency and strong resistance to post-processing.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a decorative sheet suitable for applications in which both high transparency and resistance to post-processing are required. Decorative sheets are often subjected to secondary operations such as bending, drawing, laminating, embossing, or molding after manufacture. Although a transparent resin layer is desirable because it allows an underlying pattern, color, or design to remain clearly visible, conventional transparent layers may become cloudy, whiten, crack, or otherwise deteriorate when exposed to heat or mechanical deformation during these operations.

To address this problem, the decorative sheet includes a transparent resin layer whose principal resin component is crystalline polypropylene. The molecular and crystalline state of the polypropylene is evaluated by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. In particular, peak intensities at or near 997 cm⁻¹, 973 cm⁻¹, and 938 cm⁻¹ are measured and used to calculate the peak intensity ratio x according to the following expression:

\[
x=\frac{I_{997}-I_{938}}{I_{973}-I_{938}},
\]

where \(I_{997}\), \(I_{973}\), and \(I_{938}\) represent the infrared absorption intensities at the respective wavenumbers.

The transparent resin layer is controlled so that the calculated peak intensity ratio x is 0.65 or less. This spectroscopic limitation provides an objective indicator of a polypropylene structure that achieves an advantageous balance between optical clarity and resistance to deformation or deterioration during subsequent processing. As a result, the resin layer can retain excellent transparency while suppressing defects such as whitening, clouding, cracking, or loss of surface quality when the decorative sheet is processed.

Accordingly, the invention provides a decorative sheet that clearly displays an underlying decorative pattern while maintaining durability through post-processing. The sheet is therefore particularly useful for decorative laminates, molded articles, interior and exterior finishing materials, furniture components, building materials, vehicle-interior components, and other products in which a transparent protective surface must withstand heat and mechanical forming.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention described in a patent concerning a decorative sheet whose transparent resin layer is mainly crystalline polypropylene and is characterized by infrared absorption peaks at 997, 938, and 973 cm⁻¹.
counterfactuals.output:
The patent describes a decorative sheet for surfaces such as furniture, building materials, and molded products. The sheet includes a printed or otherwise decorated substrate covered by a transparent protective resin layer composed mainly of crystalline polypropylene.

The polypropylene layer is engineered to have a particular crystalline or molecular-ordering state, identified by its infrared absorption bands near 997, 938, and 973 cm⁻¹—typically evaluated through the relative intensities of these peaks. Controlling this structure provides a better balance than conventional polypropylene films: high transparency and preservation of the underlying design, together with surface hardness, scratch and abrasion resistance, and sufficient flexibility for bending, embossing, or three-dimensional lamination. It also reduces defects such as cracking, stress whitening, or loss of appearance during fabrication.

In essence, the invention uses the specified infrared spectral characteristics as a practical definition of a specially controlled crystalline-polypropylene surface layer that gives the decorative sheet both durability and good forming/processability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a formal patent-style description of a decorative sheet (1) containing a transparent resin layer (4), where the FTIR-derived ratio x=(I997−I938)/(I973−I938) does not exceed 0.65.
counterfactuals.output:
A decorative sheet (1) comprises a transparent resin layer (4). In an infrared absorption spectrum of the transparent resin layer (4), as measured by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), when I938, I973, and I997 respectively represent spectral intensities at wavenumbers of 938 cm−1, 973 cm−1, and 997 cm−1, a ratio x calculated according to the following expression (1) is 0.65 or less:

\[
x=\frac{I_{997}-I_{938}}{I_{973}-I_{938}} \tag{1}
\]

The spectral intensities may be absorbance values obtained under identical measurement and baseline-processing conditions. The transparent resin layer (4) is arranged so that an underlying decorative pattern is visible through the transparent resin layer (4). By controlling the FTIR-derived ratio x to not more than 0.65, the transparent resin layer (4) can provide desirable optical transparency while imparting suitable surface and durability characteristics to the decorative sheet (1).

In one embodiment, the decorative sheet (1) further comprises a substrate layer and a decorative layer disposed between the substrate layer and the transparent resin layer (4). The transparent resin layer (4) may constitute an outermost surface layer or may be provided with an additional surface-protective layer, provided that the ratio x of the transparent resin layer (4) satisfies expression (1).
